doc.title: Bill Huntington and Charlie Suhor Interview, 1992-04-06

title: Burton's television and radio shows and later bass work
summary: Stories of Burton's TV and radio shows, his wife Leah, and Liston Johnson; Huntington then moves into bass at the Playboy Clubs.

Yeah, this was on radio. Live radio show. Yeah, it was incredible. And then we started doing these television shows and I remember one television show we did had Liston Johnson. Do you know who Liston is? Liston is like just a legend in himself, man. I mean, he's been around for so many years. He's one of those early people who came to New Orleans and absorbed the culture and stayed here and, I mean, was a fixture at the Fairmont for how many years, man? When it was way back when it was at Roosevelt and the Fountain Lounge. Anyway, Liston was playing tenor on this particular radio show and that morning Stan, the headline had a picture of Stan Getz robbing a drugstore in L.A. or somewhere in California and Liston was taking a chorus and Joe screams, this is on television, Joe screams from the piano, you must rob drugstores. So this is the kind of guy he was, man, really out.
